rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION ON ACCOUNT OF GENDER, SEXUAL ORIENTATION, AGE, RELIGION, ETHNIC OR CULTURAL GROUP, OR PHYSICAL APPEARANCE IN PUBLIC OR PRIVATE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES, TENURE, OR PROMOTIONS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR

rows.author: C016
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF BREWERY-MANUFAC TURING AREAS IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to allocate twenty percent (20%) of the proceeds of the excise taxes on locally manufactured or produced brewery products to the host area or local government unit where the brewery plant is located. This share of the host area or local government unit will be taken from the incremental revenue collected from the excise tax on brewery products.  The amount allotted to the host area or local government unit shall be used to finance local development projects such as infrastructure development, livelihood enhancement and environmental protection programs which shall be undertaken by registered cooperatives and organizations and the local government unit itself.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-10-15

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE INTERNAL AFFAIRS SERVICE FOR THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE TITLE V OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-ONE ENTITLED, `AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REFORM AND REORGANIZATION OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AS AMENDED' APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The passage of Republic Act 8551 (PNP Reform and Reorganization Act of 1998) creating the Internal Affairs Service of the PNP has been viewed positively as the much needed catalyst in the PNP reforms, particularly in the aspect of discipline. However, unfolding events have manifested the inadequacy of the law for the Internal Affairs Service to enable it to fully perform its mandated functions as the watchdog agency of the PNP. > Under this bill, the function of the IAS TO SERVE AS AN INDEPENDENT, IMPARTIAL AND OBJECTIVE INSTITUTIONAL WATCHDOG AGENCY FOR THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE is underscored. The bill, likewise, contains provisions AMENDING certain provisions of RA No. 8551, such as on: 1. Qualification requirements forthe IAS Head; 2. Appointments; Promotions; 3. Disciplinary decisions; and 4. Appeals.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-10-15

rows.author: D026
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR VOLUNTARY DRUG TESTING OF HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS
rows.abstract: This bill intends to help parents encourage their children who are about to enter college to voluntarily undergo testing for drug or substance abuse.  The intention of which is to prevent students from continuing further their vice while in school as it will pose more inconveniences in the future for both the parent and the child.  If tested positive for drug or substance abuse, it is the decision of the family to voluntarily refer their child to any institution that will undertake their rehabilitation. This process will be undergone in close coordination with school authorities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-10-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed IDENTIFICATION CARD shall be used in all transactions with any government agency, in filing of application for any services and benefits offered by the Government Service Insurance System, the Social Security System and the PhilHealth,in tendering or making tax payments to the concerned agency, in seeking admission to any government hospital, health centers and similar institutions, in seeking admission in all schools, whether public or private, in casting his vote during elections, whether national or local, and in such other transactions as may be provided for under the rules and regulations to be promulgated by the Department of Justice. Provided, That the ID card shall be made of hard plastic, tamper-proof/fo ol-proof andd similarly designed like the existing driver's license issued by the Land Transportation Authority. Provided, further,  That there should only be one authorized manufacturer and printer of said ID.

rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is the policy of the State to protect the interest of the consumer, promote his general welfare and establish standards of conduct for business and industry. This policy gave birth to the enactment of Republic Act No. 7394, otherwiseknown as the "Consumer Act of the Philippines". The enactment of the law demonstrates the government's commitment to protect the consumer against hazards to health and safety, deceptive, unfair and unconscionable sales acts and practices. The law also provides for the promotion of the right of consumers to information and education, product safety, and access to product that they need. Focusing at the same time on the involvement of consumers representatives in the formulation of social and econnomic policies. >Nine years after the passage of the Consumer Act however, the consumer rights advocate are discovering the flaws of the law. rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SPECIAL BENEFITS TO GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL RETIRED UNDER R.A. 660, R.A. 1616 AND P.D. 1146, WHO ARE 70 YEARS OR OLDER, BY PROVIDING NEW PROCEDURES IN THE COMPUTATION OF MONTHLY PENSIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to modify the manner of computing the monthly pension of retirees by making the salary schedule provided in Executive Order No. 389 as one of the bases. This would give substance to the provision of RA 7432 (Senior Citizens Act),particularly, Section 6 thereof, which reads: "Section 6. Retirement benefits.  To the extend practicable and feasible, retirement benefits from both the Government and the Private sector shall be upgraded at par with the current scale enjoyed by those in actual service." This bill would also allow the change of modes of retirement of those that previously retired under RA 1616 and are now 70 years or older.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-10-15

rows.author: D009
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE RESEARCH OF LOCAL HISTORIES AND INTEGRATING SUCH FINDINGS INTO THE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY CURRICULUM OF EVERY MUNICIPALITY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Local Histories Research and Curriculum Integration Act of 2001". Rationale:  At present, the Philippine educational system has integrated history into the curriculum mostly in the context of national events.  So much emphasis has been given on personalities and events at the national capital and other major cities in the country.  Yet we hardly know the very history of our own village or municipality. The present curriculum in history obviously lacks the necessary information at the local level. This dent of information has consequently created a gap in the political consciousness of our youth. Thus this bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-10-16

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT FIXING THE RETIREMENT AGE OF MILITARY PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The age of compulsory retirement of enlisted personnel is hereby fixed at 56 years. Military officers shall be compulsorily retired at the age of 58 years: Provided, That a Major General, a Lieutenant General and a fulkl-fledged General shall each be granted another year of service before retirement. The rationale of this Act is to be able to maximize the services of highly qualified, highly competent, and highly trained officers as they must have assumed key positions in the AFP hierarchical order. For studies have proven that military officers are very good economic managers whose expertise and services just cannot be dispensed with.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04419
